title: Number of Different Integers in a String
summary: Given a string that includes digits and lowercase English letters, replace every non-digit character with a space.
statement: Given a string that includes digits and lowercase English letters, replace every non-digit character with a space. For example, the string "a123bc34d8ef34" will be transformed into " 123 34 8 34". After this transformation, count the number of unique integers that are formed, where integers are considered unique if their decimal representations, without leading zeros, are different.
constraints: Maximal digit runs form the integers; letters separate runs.
Ignore leading zeros when comparing values, with every all-zero run representing zero.
hints: Letters split the input into maximal digit runs.
Normalize each run by stripping leading zeros, using 0 for an empty remainder.
Insert normalized runs into a set and return its size.
Decimal strings without leading zeros are unique representations, so set equality is exactly integer equality without requiring large numeric conversion.
editorial: Decimal strings without leading zeros are unique representations, so set equality is exactly integer equality without requiring large numeric conversion.

tests.explanation: The runs represent 123, 34, 8, and 34, giving three distinct integers.
All three runs represent integer one after removing leading zeros.
